nodes.label: Ports (core/ports.ts seams)
nodes.rationale: Each port interface is kept small enough to fake in a test and to fill from an npm package; they are the seams between the pure core and anything that touches hardware, a model or the network.

nodes.label: core/builtins.ts as the only core-to-providers import
nodes.rationale: Nothing in core imports providers except builtins.ts, which only registers the built-ins; a program embedding Parlour with its own providers can leave that one file out.

nodes.label: Provider registry keyed by (kind, name)
nodes.rationale: Core only knows the provider key of each config slice; the rest passes through to the provider's own Zod schema so core has no idea Kokoro has a voice. An unregistered name is tried as an npm package via await import(name), which is the entire extension mechanism. secrets and service are picked by platform rather than config.

nodes.label: buildAgent assembly
nodes.rationale: The mic loop, text REPL, doctor and network server all take one Agent rather than building their own, so a timer set from a phone still sounds in the room and every client shares one tool list. A provider that cannot start (missing key) is reported by the doctor and left out, but a name that leads nowhere is thrown, because a house that quietly answers with the wrong model is worse than one that refuses to start.

nodes.label: Speaker (TTS + sink + sentence splitting)
nodes.rationale: Composed in core rather than left to a provider. The reply is rendered and played one sentence at a time so the first words come out while the rest is still being made.

nodes.label: FallbackTextToSpeech
nodes.rationale: Wraps two voices, uses the second when the first throws, warns once and retries the first on the next sentence. Default fallback is macos-say so a Kokoro that has not finished downloading still speaks. Lives in core, not inside the Kokoro provider.

nodes.label: Timers in core
nodes.rationale: The one tool that has to keep working when the network does not, so it lives in core and announces through the Speaker.

nodes.label: Voice session state machine (idle/listening/thinking/speaking)
nodes.rationale: One state machine over a stream of 80 ms frames that does not care where frames come from: local mic, satellite, phone or custom hardware all feed the same object. Frames arriving while speaking reset the wake word instead of being listened to unless audio.bargeIn is on, because with one box in one room the microphone hears the speaker. Clients that know their own request boundaries call utterance(frames) and skip wake and endpointing.

nodes.label: Per-client sessions keyed by client id
nodes.rationale: Every client has its own session so a follow-up in the kitchen cannot pick up something asked in the study; history is forgotten after four minutes of silence.

nodes.label: Endpointer
nodes.rationale: Gives up after 2.5 s of leading silence, finishes after audio.silenceMs of quiet once speech has started, caps a request at audio.maxUtteranceMs.

nodes.label: Router (local first, cloud escalation)
nodes.rationale: The local model gets the prompt, the tools and ask_the_clever_one; when it calls it, the rewritten question and history go to the cloud model, which has server-side web search and no house tools. If local throws or times out and llm.cloud.onLocalFailure is true, cloud gets the original question. With no cloud model, failures are final and the escalation tool is not offered.

nodes.label: Tool rounds loop (core/loop.ts)
nodes.rationale: Runs the tool rounds for whichever model is answering, up to llm.maxToolRounds, and stops with an apology rather than looping forever.

nodes.label: config.json Zod schema with defaults for every key
nodes.rationale: Every key has a default, so an empty file is a complete config and parlour config show prints what is in force.

nodes.label: secrets.env (mode 600, env wins)
nodes.rationale: HA_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, PARLOUR_TOKEN, BRAVE_API_KEY, LOG_LEVEL stay in secrets.env with mode 600; the process environment wins over the file so a one-off run can override without editing.

nodes.label: Paths (PARLOUR_HOME, PARLOUR_CONFIG, caches, logs, XDG on Linux)
--events NDJSON stream (ready, state, heard, reply, muted, error)
nodes.rationale: One JSON line per state change on stdout so the desktop app draws its status from structured events rather than scraping log text.

nodes.label: parlour doctor (concatenated Check[])
nodes.rationale: Every configured part's doctor() checks joined together, plus three of core's own: config parses, the network is let in, something keeps Parlour running.

nodes.label: Each stage chosen to be fast rather than best
nodes.source_location: ## Why the pieces are the pieces
nodes.rationale: Latency adds up across wake, capture, STT, model, speech, so every stage is picked for speed; the cloud model is the safety net for correctness. Being wrong out loud is expensive; handing over is cheap.

nodes.label: openWakeWord (ONNX, in process)
nodes.source_location: ## Why the pieces are the pieces
nodes.rationale: Free, offline, and runs in the same Node process as everything else, which is what makes barge-in possible.

nodes.label: ffmpeg on avfoundation capture
nodes.source_location: ## Why the pieces are the pieces
nodes.rationale: Nothing to compile, and the only reliable way to pin one input device on macOS.

nodes.label: whisper.cpp small.en kept warm as a server
nodes.source_location: ## Why the pieces are the pieces
nodes.rationale: Loading the model costs more than transcribing a sentence, so it runs as a server (a separate LaunchAgent, io.parlour.whisper).

nodes.label: LM Studio MLX local model over OpenAI API
nodes.source_location: ## Why the pieces are the pieces
nodes.rationale: Fastest way to run an 8B model on Apple silicon, and it speaks the OpenAI API so the runtime stays swappable.

nodes.label: Claude with server-side web search as escalation
nodes.source_location: ## Why the pieces are the pieces
nodes.rationale: The local model is fast and private but wrong more often. Handing over is cheap; being wrong out loud is not.

nodes.label: Kokoro 82M ONNX voice
nodes.source_location: ## Why the pieces are the pieces
nodes.rationale: Close to a cloud voice, runs in process, and has British voices. macOS say is the fallback for when it fails.
